newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed to brief Chernomyrdin on Chechnya - agencies.
newsitem.headline: Lebed to brief Chernomyrdin on Chechnya - agencies.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed will brief Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday on his talks with Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, Russian news agencies said.
The agencies quoted Lebed as saying Tuesday's talks with Yandarbiyev had been "highly successful".
Lebed pledged Moscow would press ahead with a planned troop withdrawal from Chechnya which was suspended by army commanders last week.
It was not clear if Lebed would meet Chernomyrdin in person. The prime minister was due in St Petersburg for talks with the organisers of the city's bid to stage the 2004 Olympic Games.
"Even by the end of the week, Viktor Chernomyrdin will get personally involved in the negotiating process," Interfax news agency quoted Lebed as saying.
It was not clear if that meant Chernomyrdin, who has taken on extra responsibilities as doctors prepare President Boris Yeltsin for heart surgery, would meet separatist leaders.
Lebed, a former paratroop general, had harsh words for the Russian commanders in the region, whom he met on Tuesday before his talks with the separatists.
Itar-Tass news agency said Lebed was "fed up with the situation in which the command makes announcements like that on the suspension of the troop withdrawal".
But Lebed said he had reached agreement with army commander General Vyacheslav Tikhomirov. "I hope we will have no more of such falling out of step," he said.
Lebed said Yandarbiyev had agreed Russian law should operate across Chechnya. There was no confirmation from the separatists, who have introduced Islamic sharia law in the region.

Both sides confirmed their commitment to last month's peace deal. Lebed said they would push ahead with the demilitarisation of the Chechen capital Grozny and had agreed in principle on forming a coalition government in Chechnya -- a potential sticking point.
A meeting to discuss the formation of the new government last week was boycotted by Chechnya's pro-Moscow leader, Doku Zavgayev, who says it is too early to talk about a coalition.
Interfax quoted an Interior Ministry spokesman as saying there was one shooting incident in Chechnya overnight. No soldiers were injured.
